topic: Ten leading companies relevant to film and television acting careers (US and UK), with corporate status as of October 2026
criteria: Companies were weighed on four things. (1) Production activity: whether the company itself develops and produces scripted film and television, and how much (films released per year, series in production). (2) Distribution reach: domestic (US/Canada) and UK-Ireland theatrical market share in 2025, and the last-published streaming subscriber count. (3) Commissioning influence: whether the company orders scripted series and films from other producers (a commissioner hires actors indirectly through its producers). (4) Relevance to an actor in New York, Los Angeles or London: membership of the AMPTP (the producers' bargaining group whose agreement with SAG-AFTRA covers US film and TV acting), a published Equity agreement in the UK, and owned or long-leased studio facilities in Los Angeles, the New York area or the London studio belt. Scale counts but is not decisive; a smaller company that is a major direct engager of UK actors (ITV) can outrank a larger one that mainly finances. This is a defensible working selection for a game world, NOT a universal ranking: the order is not a ranking, other reasonable lists exist, and several numbers are company-reported or last-published figures that the companies have since stopped disclosing.
scope: Primary markets: United States (Los Angeles and New York) and United Kingdom (London and the wider UK). Units are counted once at the parent level, except where noted: NBCUniversal is listed under its parent Comcast; Sky (UK) is a division of Comcast; BBC Studios is a division of the BBC; ITV is listed at ITV plc level with ITV Studios as the part that survives the pending Sky deal; Sony Pictures Entertainment is chosen as the unit rather than Sony Group because Sony Group's other businesses (electronics, games, music) are not film/TV employers; Amazon MGM Studios and Apple's TV/studio unit are chosen as units rather than Amazon.com and Apple Inc. for the same reason. Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery are counted as ONE company, Skydance Corporation, because the acquisition closed on 2026-10-06. Other markets noted where relevant: Canada (Toronto, Vancouver), New Mexico (Albuquerque), Wales (Cardiff), Northern England (Salford/Manchester).

selection.name: The Walt Disney Company
selection.whyChosen: Largest US distributor by 2025 domestic box office share (27.5%) and the highest global studio gross in 2025 ($6.58bn); second in UK-Ireland (23.1%). Owns studios, broadcast and cable networks and two large streaming services (Disney+, Hulu, now wholly owned). AMPTP member through Walt Disney Studios and ABC. Holds a long-term lease on most of Pinewood Studios near London, where Lucasfilm shot Andor. CEO changed to Josh D'Amaro on 2026-03-18.

selection.name: Apple TV / Apple Studios (Apple Original Films)
selection.whyChosen: A high-budget commissioner and producer of scripted series and films, notably of UK-made series (Slow Horses) and New York-area productions (Severance). selection.name: Lionsgate Studios Corp.
selection.whyChosen: The largest standalone 'pure play' studio outside the conglomerates: it released 24 films theatrically in the US in the fiscal year to March 2026, holds a library of over 20,000 titles, self-distributes in the UK and Ireland through Lionsgate UK, and owns the talent management and production company 3 Arts. It became fully independent of Starz in May 2025. It is NOT an AMPTP member, which is why its films could use SAG-AFTRA interim agreements in the 2023 strike: a materially different relationship with the actors' union. Takeover interest from Banijay and Mediawan was reported in July 2026; no deal confirmed.

excluded.why: Existed 2025-08-07 to 2026-10-06; restructured as Skydance Corporation on the WBD closing. Counted once, as Skydance Corporation.

excluded.name: A24
excluded.why: Influential New York independent (valued at $3.5bn in 2024) with strong awards-season relevance, but releases far fewer films than Lionsgate, owns no streaming service or studio facilities found in this research, and no full-year 2025 domestic share above about 7% was found. Lionsgate was preferred as the single 'independent' slot on volume.

excluded.name: Legendary Entertainment
excluded.why: A financier and producer (Dune, Godzilla) that relies on other studios for distribution; it does not commission series or run a network. Its reported 2025 interest in buying Lionsgate did not result in a deal.

excluded.name: Banijay Entertainment (now including All3Media)
excluded.why: The world's largest independent producer since the merger completed on 2026-07-09 (London HQ, 25 countries, over €4.3bn combined 2025 revenue), but its output is weighted toward unscripted formats; it neither distributes theatrically nor runs a channel. A strong candidate for an 11th place.

excluded.name: Fremantle (RTL Group / Bertelsmann)
excluded.why: London-based producer and distributor whose catalogue is dominated by non-scripted formats (Got Talent, Idols, The X Factor); its scripted drama business is growing but is smaller than the chosen broadcasters' or studios'.

excluded.name: Versant Media Group
excluded.why: Spun off from Comcast on 2026-01-02; a cable-network company (MS NOW, CNBC, USA Network, E!, SYFY, Oxygen, Golf Channel) whose schedules are mostly news, sport and unscripted, with little scripted commissioning.

excluded.name: Starz Entertainment
excluded.why: Separated from Lionsgate in May 2025; a premium channel and streamer of smaller scale that commissions fewer series than the chosen streamers.

excluded.name: Sky Group (as a separate entry)
excluded.why: Wholly owned by Comcast, so counted inside Comcast to avoid double-counting; it is, however, the most important UK commissioner after the BBC and ITV, and owns Sky Studios Elstree.

excluded.name: Channel 4
excluded.why: A publisher-broadcaster that commissions but by design does not produce in-house, and has a smaller drama budget than the BBC or ITV. Not researched in depth here.

excluded.name: Mediawan
excluded.why: A French producer expanding into English-language production (it acquired North Road / Chernin Entertainment); reported July 2026 interest in Lionsgate, unconfirmed. Not yet at the US/UK scale of the chosen ten.
